description: we are a team of junior CS students from FCAI-BSU
summary:
Skytime is a web tool for looking at the same patch of sky in several SPHEREx infrared images. You pick one of five preset objects (Barnard’s Star, Epsilon Indi B, WISE 0855, RW Aurigae, R Draconis) or type sky coordinates. 

Skytime fetches small cutouts of real SPHEREx images from NASA/IPAC IRSA and lets you play them as a “blink”, scrub through them, or view a difference against the
first frame. It targets the SPHEREx challenge: making SPHEREx data easier for students and non-experts to explore and compare over time. It is a working prototype. It does not detect moving objects or Planet X automatically, and in its current form most
patches return frames from a single observing day, so it shows how the viewer works rather than proving any discovery.
details:
What it does. The user chooses a target or enters RA/Dec (decimal degrees, J2000) and a field of view (0.01 to 0.5 degrees,

default 0.1). Skytime returns up to six real SPHEREx cutouts for that position, ordered by observation time, and shows them in a

viewer with play/pause, a frame scrubber, speed control, and two modes: Blink (show frames one after another) and Difference

(subtract the first frame taken by the same detector from the current frame, computed in the browser). Each frame is labelled with

its date, detector number and wavelength range.

How it works. Three parts: 1. Frontend: React + Vite single-page app (nasa-front/). 2. Backend API: ASP.NET Core (.NET 10)

(Controllers/, Services/). It validates input, caches results, returns a consistent error format, and talks to the image service.

Endpoints: GET /api/frames, GET /api/frames/{id}/image, GET /api/targets, plus sample catalog routes. The contract

is in API_CONTRACT.md. 3. Image service: Python FastAPI with astropy (image-service/). It searches the public IRSA SIA2

service for SPHEREx DR1 and QR3 images covering the position, requests a small FITS cutout for each, orients it north-up/east-left

from the FITS WCS, converts it to an 8-bit PNG (1st to 99.5th percentile stretch), and caches it.

The backend also has a mock mode that returns generated, clearly labelled “SIMULATED” frames. It exists so the front end can be

developed and demoed without the archive. Real mode is the default.

Benefits and goals. Lower the effort needed to look at multi-visit SPHEREx data: no FITS tools, no archive query forms, one click

per target. Longer-term goal: help people spot sources that move or change between SPHEREx visits.

Tools. React, Vite, framer-motion, lucide-react (frontend); C#/.NET 10 (API); Python, FastAPI, astropy, numpy, Pillow, requests

(image service); Azure App Service (image-service hosting, per the deployment config in the repo); Netlify config for the front end is

in the repo.

What works now. Searching IRSA for SPHEREx images at a position and rendering cutouts; blink/scrub/difference viewing; five

presets; custom coordinates; error and loading states; caching; mock mode.

Limits (please read). - Each query returns at most six frames. In the cached queries we checked for the five preset targets, four

returned frames from a single day (alternating between two detectors, i.e. two wavelength bands) and one (R Draconis) spanned

two dates a few days apart. So Skytime currently shows exposures hours to days apart, not months-apart epochs, and a slowly

moving star will not visibly move. - Frames from different detectors are different wavelength bands, so brightness changesbetween them mostly reflect colour, not change over time. - Images are 8-bit with an independent percentile stretch per frame.

The Difference mode subtracts these stretched images; it is a visual aid, not calibrated photometry. - There is no automatic

detection of moving objects, no machine learning, and no Planet X search. A person has to look. - WISE 0855 is extremely faint in

SPHEREx bands; we do not claim to see it in our cutouts. - The first request for a new position can take up to about a minute

If the backend is unreachable the page falls back to a procedural local preview that is not real data.

Future plans (not built). More visits per target across the 6-month survey cycles; calibrated flux difference images; real spectra

from SPHEREx spectral data; automatic candidate flagging; filtering by detector (reserved in the API contract).
